title: Tell me about yourself
interviewAnswer: Use a 60–90 second present → past → future structure. Start with your current professional identity, connect 2–3 relevant experiences, and end with the type of problem you want to solve next. Do not narrate the entire CV.
keyPoints: Choose experiences that support the target role
why: This opening answer sets the frame for the rest of the interview. A good version directs the interviewer toward the experiences you most want to discuss.
intuition: Do not recite the CV. Give a short professional story: where you are now, the two or three experiences that explain how you got there, and what type of work you want next.
deepDive: A 60–90 second answer is usually enough. Start with your current role/study, move backward through only the experiences relevant to the target role, then close with a forward bridge. Mention the company only lightly unless the interviewer combines this question with “why us?”. Keep technical nouns concrete but avoid architecture-level detail.
workedExample: Current role/study → one or two relevant past experiences → the theme connecting them → what kind of problem or responsibility you want next.
commonMistakes: Starting with childhood or a full chronological biography.
Repeating every bullet on the resume.
Turning the answer into a long “why this company” speech before being asked.
followUps: Why did you move from data engineering to data science?
Which experience shaped your interests most?
What kind of problems do you want to work on?
production: Treat this as your interview routing layer: the projects you mention are the ones most likely to receive follow-up questions, so only mention claims you are ready to defend.
